name: Pima Indians Diabetes Diagnostic
tagline: Predict diabetes onset while handling disguised zero-sentinel physiological missingness.
description:
Compiled by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) from longitudinal epidemiological studies of Akimel O'odham (Gila River Indian Community) women aged 21 and older near Phoenix, Arizona, and introduced to machine learning by Smith et al. (1988), this 768-patient dataset predicts World Health Organization (WHO) 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test positivity.

Pima Diabetes is the canonical benchmark in machine learning education for disguised missing data: although the raw CSV contains zero explicit empty or 'NA' cells, five physiological variables—plasma glucose (5), diastolic blood pressure (35), triceps skinfold thickness (227), 2-hour serum insulin (374), and BMI (11)—encode unrecorded lab measurements as biologically impossible 0s, whereas 0 in 'preg' is a valid count of zero pregnancies. Equally important, its single-sex, single-community sampling frame provides an essential case study in external validity limits and Indigenous Data Sovereignty.

targetCandidates.description: Predict WHO-criteria diabetes mellitus status ('tested_positive' vs. 'tested_negative').

columns.name: preg
columns.description: Number of times pregnant (note: 0 is a valid clinical count for nulliparous patients, NOT a missing value).

columns.name: plas
columns.description: Plasma glucose concentration at 2 hours in an oral glucose tolerance test; 0 in 5 rows represents unrecorded lab values.

columns.name: pres
columns.description: Resting diastolic arterial blood pressure; 0 in 35 rows is physiologically impossible in living patients and denotes missingness.

columns.name: skin
columns.description: Triceps skinfold thickness measured via caliper; 0 in 227 rows (29.6%) denotes unmeasured values.

columns.name: insu
columns.description: 2-hour post-load serum insulin concentration; 0 in 374 rows (48.7%) denotes unmeasured assays.

columns.name: mass
columns.description: Body mass index (weight in kg divided by height in m squared); 0 in 11 rows denotes missing height/weight.

columns.name: pedi
columns.description: Composite genetic-family history risk score synthesizing diabetes incidence and age of onset across relatives.

columns.name: age
columns.description: Patient age in years (sample restricted to women aged 21 and older; diabetes prevalence is 21.2% under age 30 vs. 49.5% aged 30+).

columns.name: class
columns.description: Diagnostic indicator of WHO-criteria diabetes mellitus (2-hour post-load plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dL).

creators: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)

warnings: Sampled exclusively from Akimel O'odham (Pima) women aged >= 21; models trained on this cohort lack external validity for men, youth, or broader demographic populations.

Historian Joanna Radin (2017) documents how mid-20th-century biomedical data from the Gila River Indian Community became a decontextualized ML benchmark without ongoing community governance—an essential teaching case for Indigenous Data Sovereignty and the CARE Principles.
